title: Arterial Territories & Stroke Comparison
subtitle: Compare ACA, MCA, PCA, perforator and posterior-circulation lesion patterns
altText: Interactive chalkboard-style anatomical map of Arterial Territories & Stroke Comparison with selectable regions and pathways.
learningObjectives: Identify the major components of the Arterial Territories & Stroke Comparison.
Trace key inputs, outputs and connections in the Arterial Territories & Stroke Comparison.
Interpret lesion patterns cautiously using distributed-network and clinical context.

sections.explainSimply: Compare ACA, MCA, PCA, perforator and posterior-circulation lesion patterns.
sections.explainLikePsychologist: Post-stroke mood, fatigue, apathy and cognitive change reflect lesion location, network disconnection, systemic illness, disability and psychosocial context rather than a single “stroke personality.”
sections.advancedClinicalDetail: Location: Arterial territories cover cortical surfaces, deep nuclei, white matter, brainstem and cerebellum with substantial anatomical variation and collateral overlap. Major subdivisions include anterior cerebral artery territory, middle cerebral artery territory, posterior cerebral artery territory, lenticulostriate arteries, anterior choroidal artery, posterior inferior cerebellar artery, anterior inferior cerebellar artery, superior cerebellar artery, basilar perforators. Inputs include internal carotid circulation, vertebrobasilar circulation, circle of Willis collateral routes; outputs include cortical branches, deep perforators, brainstem and cerebellar branches.
sections.thinkOfItLike: A dynamic transport and control map: the meaning of any node depends on the routes entering, leaving and bypassing it.
sections.whyPsychologistsCare: Post-stroke mood, fatigue, apathy and cognitive change reflect lesion location, network disconnection, systemic illness, disability and psychosocial context rather than a single “stroke personality.”
sections.whenItGoesWrong: Ischaemia or haemorrhage may produce contralateral motor/sensory deficits, aphasia, neglect, visual-field loss, memory disturbance, ataxia, cranial-nerve findings or altered consciousness depending on site and extent.
sections.clinicalPearl: Time plus territory matters: sudden focal deficit is vascular until proven otherwise, and urgent stroke pathways outrank elegant localisation.
sections.practicalExample: Select a region, trace its incoming and outgoing pathways, then compare healthy and lesion overlays before forming a clinical hypothesis.
sections.limitationsCautions: Classic syndromes are teaching heuristics. Real strokes cross boundaries, spare expected regions, evolve over time and are modified by collaterals, reperfusion and prior brain health.

anatomy.position: Arterial territories cover cortical surfaces, deep nuclei, white matter, brainstem and cerebellum with substantial anatomical variation and collateral overlap.
anatomy.spatialRelationships: Interpreted relative to connected cortical, subcortical and vascular structures; boundaries and laterality must be checked in the selected view.
anatomy.bloodSupply: This atlas is itself a vascular map. Territory boundaries are approximate and vary with branching patterns, dominance and collateral circulation.
anatomy.lesionEffects: Ischaemia or haemorrhage may produce contralateral motor/sensory deficits, aphasia, neglect, visual-field loss, memory disturbance, ataxia, cranial-nerve findings or altered consciousness depending on site and extent.
anatomy.clinicalSignificance: Post-stroke mood, fatigue, apathy and cognitive change reflect lesion location, network disconnection, systemic illness, disability and psychosocial context rather than a single “stroke personality.”

quiz.question: A dominant-hemisphere superior-division MCA stroke most classically threatens:
options: Expressive language and face-arm motor systems
quiz.rationale: The dominant lateral frontal territory includes language-production and face-arm motor regions, though actual patterns vary.

quiz.question: Why are arterial territory maps approximate?
options: Branching, dominance and collateral circulation vary between individuals
quiz.rationale: Individual vascular anatomy and collateral flow shift functional territory boundaries.

quiz.question: What is the safest response to sudden new facial weakness and speech disturbance?
options: Use lesion localisation as definitive diagnosis
quiz.rationale: Acute focal neurological deficits require emergency medical assessment because treatment is time-sensitive.
